WalkthroughText: A while loop repeats a block of code as long as its condition stays true. Java checks the condition first, before running the loop body at all — if the condition is false right away, the body never executes. Each time through the loop (called an iteration), some variable used in the condition usually gets updated; if it never changes in a way that eventually makes the condition false, you get an infinite loop. Tracing a while loop means watching one variable's value change in memory while you repeatedly jump back to the condition line.

PracticeItems.Explanation: count starts at 1 (prints, since 1<5), becomes 3 (prints, since 3<5), becomes 5, and now 5<5 is false so the loop stops. Only 1 and 3 are printed. '1 3 5 ' is wrong because once count is 5, the condition fails before printing again.

Choices: The loop condition uses < instead of <=
The variable i is never updated inside the loop body
The while loop needs a semicolon after the condition
PracticeItems.Explanation: Since i is never changed inside the loop body, the condition i < 5 stays true forever. Using <= would actually make it run one extra time, not fix the infinite loop, and print vs println doesn't affect whether the loop terminates.

WalkthroughSteps.Caption: Here is our while loop. We declare an int variable count and set it to 1, before the loop even starts.
Now we reach the while line. Java checks the condition count < 4 using the current value of count, which is 1.
Since the condition is true, we enter the loop body and print count's value, which is 1.
Next line updates count by adding 1 to it, so count changes from 1 to 2 in memory.
The loop body has finished, so control jumps back up to the while line to re-check the condition with count now 2.
True again, so we repeat the body: print 2, then update count from 2 to 3.
Back to the while line one more time. Now count is 3, and 3 < 4 is still true, so we go around again.
We print 3, then update count from 3 to 4.
Control jumps back to the while line one final time. Now count is 4, and 4 < 4 is false.
Because the condition is now false, the loop stops immediately and execution moves to the line after the closing brace, having printed 1, 2, 3.
